163.s: kim̐svidāsīdadhi̱ṣṭhāna̍māra̱mbhaṇa̍ṃ kata̱matsvitka̱thāsī̍t yato̱ bhūmi̍ṃ ja̱naya̍nvi̱śvaka̍rmā̱ vi dyāmorṇo̍nmahi̱nā vi̱śvaca̍kṣā:
163.d: किम्̐स्विदासीदधि̱ष्ठान̍मार̱म्भण̍ं कत̱मत्स्वित्क̱थासी̍त् यतो̱ भूमि̍ं ज̱नय̍न्वि̱श्वक̍र्मा̱ वि द्यामोर्णो̍न्महि̱ना वि̱श्वच̍क्षा:
163.m: What indeed was the standing-place, what was the starting point, of what kind was it, / from which Viśvakarman, generating the earth, disclosed heaven by his greatness, seeing all?

163.s: vi̱śvata̍ścakṣuru̱ta vi̱śvato̍mukho vi̱śvato̍bāhuru̱ta vi̱śvata̍spāt saṃ bā̱hubhyā̱ṃ dhama̍ti̱ saṃ pata̍trairdyāvā̱bhūmī̍ ja̱naya̍nde̱va eka̍:
163.d: वि̱श्वत̍श्चक्षुरु̱त वि̱श्वतो̍मुखो वि̱श्वतो̍बाहुरु̱त वि̱श्वत̍स्पात् सं बा̱हुभ्या̱ं धम̍ति̱ सं पत̍त्रैर्द्यावा̱भूमी̍ ज̱नय̍न्दे̱व एक̍:
163.m: With eyes on all sides, with faces on all sides, with arms on all sides, and with feet on all sides, / blowing together with his arms, together with his wings, the one god, generating heaven and earth.

163.s: kim̐svidvana̱ṃ ka u̱ sa vṛ̱kṣa ā̍sa̱ yato̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī ni̍ṣṭata̱kṣu: manī̍ṣiṇo̱ mana̍sā pṛ̱cchatedu̱ tadyada̱dhyati̍ṣṭha̱dbhuva̍nāni dhā̱raya̍n
163.d: किम्̐स्विद्वन̱ं क उ̱ स वृ̱क्ष आ̍स̱ यतो̱ द्यावा̍पृथि̱वी नि̍ष्टत̱क्षु: मनी̍षिणो̱ मन̍सा पृ̱च्छतेदु̱ तद्यद̱ध्यति̍ष्ठ̱द्भुव̍नानि धा̱रय̍न्
163.m: What indeed was the forest, and what was that tree from which they carved out heaven and earth? / Inquire into that with your mind, O wise men, upon what he stood while upholding the worlds.

163.s: yā te̱ dhāmā̍ni para̱māṇi̱ yāva̱mā yā ma̍dhya̱mā vi̍śvakarma̱nnutemā śikṣā̱ sakhi̍bhyo ha̱viṣi̍ svadhāvaḥ sva̱yaṃ ya̍jasva ta̱nva̍ṃ vṛdhā̱naḥ
163.d: या ते̱ धामा̍नि पर̱माणि̱ याव̱मा या म̍ध्य̱मा वि̍श्वकर्म̱न्नुतेमा शिक्षा̱ सखि̍भ्यो ह̱विषि̍ स्वधावः स्व̱यं य̍जस्व त̱न्व̍ं वृधा̱नः
163.m: Those highest abodes of yours, O Viśvakarman, those lowest, and those intermediate ones here— / grant them to your comrades at the oblation, O self-dependent one; sacrifice yourself, growing in your body!

163.s: vā̱caspati̍ṃ vi̱śvaka̍rmāṇamū̱taye̍ mano̱juva̱ṃ vāje̍ a̱dyā hu̍vema sa no̱ viśvā̍ni̱ hava̍nāni joṣadvi̱śvaśa̍mbhūrava̍se sādhu̱karmā̍
163.d: वा̱चस्पति̍ं वि̱श्वक̍र्माणमू̱तये̍ मनो̱जुव̱ं वाजे̍ अ̱द्या हु̍वेम स नो̱ विश्वा̍नि̱ हव̍नानि जोषद्वि̱श्वश̍म्भूरव̍से साधु̱कर्मा̍
163.m: Today we would summon for help Vācaspati, Viśvakarman, swift as thought, in the contest; / may he, bringing welfare to all for our protection, doing good deeds, take pleasure in all our invocations.

163.s: vi̱śvaka̍rman ha̱viṣā̍ vāvṛdhā̱naḥ sva̱yaṃ ya̍jasva pṛthi̱vīmu̱ta dyām muhya̍ntva̱nye a̱bhita̍ḥ sa̱patnā̍ i̱hāsmāka̍ṃ ma̱ghavā̍ sū̱rira̍stu
163.d: वि̱श्वक̍र्मन् ह̱विषा̍ वावृधा̱नः स्व̱यं य̍जस्व पृथि̱वीमु̱त द्याम् मुह्य̍न्त्व̱न्ये अ̱भित̍ः स̱पत्ना̍ इ̱हास्माक̍ं म̱घवा̍ सू̱रिर̍स्तु
163.m: O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, sacrifice yourself to earth and heaven. / Let other rivals all around be confounded; here let the bounteous Maghavan be our patron.

163.s: vi̱śvaka̍rman ha̱viṣā̱ vardha̍nena trā̱tāra̱mindra̍makṛṇorava̱dhyam tasmai̱ viśa̱ḥ sama̍namanta pū̱rvīraya̍mu̱gro vi̱havyo̍ yathāsa̍t
163.d: वि̱श्वक̍र्मन् ह̱विषा̱ वर्ध̍नेन त्रा̱तार̱मिन्द्र̍मकृणोरव̱ध्यम् तस्मै̱ विश̱ः सम̍नमन्त पू̱र्वीरय̍मु̱ग्रो वि̱हव्यो̍ यथास̍त्
163.m: O Viśvakarman, through the strengthening oblation you made Indra an invincible savior. / To him the many clans bowed down, that this fierce one might be invoked by all.

164.s: (2) cakṣu̍ṣaḥ pi̱tā mana̍sā̱ hi dhīro̍ ghṛ̱tame̍ne ajana̱nnanna̍māne ya̱dedantā̱ ada̍dṛhanta̱ pūrva̱ ādiddyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̍prathetām
164.d: (2) चक्षु̍षः पि̱ता मन̍सा̱ हि धीरो̍ घृ̱तमे̍ने अजन̱न्नन्न̍माने य̱देदन्ता̱ अद̍दृहन्त̱ पूर्व̱ आदिद्द्यावा̍पृथि̱वी अ̍प्रथेताम्
164.m: Father of the eye, wise in mind, he generated these two bowing down, rich in butter, / when their former boundaries were firmly fixed; then heaven and earth spread out.

164.s: vi̱śvaka̍rmā vi̱manā̱ ād vihā̍yā dhā̱tā vi̍dhā̱tā pa̍ra̱mota sa̱ṃdṛk teṣā̍mi̱ṣṭāni̱ sami̱ṣā ma̍danti̱ yatrā̍ sa̱pta ṛṣīnpa̱ra eka̍mā̱huḥ
164.d: वि̱श्वक̍र्मा वि̱मना̱ आद् विहा̍या धा̱ता वि̍धा̱ता प̍र̱मोत स̱ंदृक् तेषा̍मि̱ष्टानि̱ समि̱षा म̍दन्ति̱ यत्रा̍ स̱प्त ऋषीन्प̱र एक̍मा̱हुः
164.m: Viśvakarman, of vast mind and wide expanse, is the creator, the disposer, and the supreme vision. / Their offerings rejoice together with food, where they speak of the One beyond the Seven Seers.

164.s: yo na̍ḥ pi̱tā ja̍ni̱tā yo vi̍dhā̱tā dhāmā̍ni̱ veda̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ viśvā̍ yo de̱vānā̍ṃ nāma̱dhā eka̍ e̱va tam̐ sa̱ṃpraśna̱ṃ bhuva̍nā yantya̱nyā
164.d: यो न̍ः पि̱ता ज̍नि̱ता यो वि̍धा̱ता धामा̍नि̱ वेद̱ भुव̍नानि̱ विश्वा̍ यो दे̱वाना̍ं नाम̱धा एक̍ ए̱व तम्̐ स̱ंप्रश्न̱ं भुव̍ना यन्त्य̱न्या
164.m: He who is our father, generator, and disposer, who knows all places and all worlds, / who alone is the name-giver of the gods—to him all other worlds go to question him.

164.s: ta ā̱yaja̍nta̱ dravi̍ṇam̐ sama̍smā̱ ṛṣa̍ya̱ḥ pūrve̍ jari̱tāro̱ na bhū̱nā asū̍rte̱ sūrte̱ raja̍si niṣa̱tte ye bhū̱tāni̍ sama̱kṛ̍ṇvanni̱māni̍
164.d: त आ̱यज̍न्त̱ द्रवि̍णम्̐ सम̍स्मा̱ ऋष̍य̱ः पूर्वे̍ जरि̱तारो̱ न भू̱ना असू̍र्ते̱ सूर्ते̱ रज̍सि निष̱त्ते ये भू̱तानि̍ सम̱कृ̍ण्वन्नि̱मानि̍
164.m: They offered wealth together to him, the ancient seers, as singers, with abundance, / they who, seated in the unseen and seen space, created these beings.

164.s: pa̱ro di̱vā pa̱ra e̱nā pṛ̍thi̱vyā pa̱ro de̱vebhi̱rasu̍rairya̱dasti̍ kam̐svi̱d garbha̍ṃ pratha̱maṃ da̍dhra̱ āpo̱ yatra̍ de̱vāḥ sa̱mapa̍śyanta̱ pūrve̍
164.d: प̱रो दि̱वा प̱र ए̱ना पृ̍थि̱व्या प̱रो दे̱वेभि̱रसु̍रैर्य̱दस्ति̍ कम्̐स्वि̱द् गर्भ̍ं प्रथ̱मं द̍ध्र̱ आपो̱ यत्र̍ दे̱वाः स̱मप̍श्यन्त̱ पूर्वे̍
164.m: Beyond heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and asuras that exist— / what first embryo did the waters hold, wherein the first gods beheld one another?

164.s: tamidgarbha̍ṃ pratha̱maṃ da̍dhra̱ āpo̱ yatra̍ de̱vāḥ sa̱maga̍cchanta̱ viśve̍ a̱jasya̱ nābhā̱ adhyeka̱marpi̍ta̱ṃ yasmi̱n viśvā̍ni̱ bhuva̍nāni ta̱sthuḥ
164.d: तमिद्गर्भ̍ं प्रथ̱मं द̍ध्र̱ आपो̱ यत्र̍ दे̱वाः स̱मग̍च्छन्त̱ विश्वे̍ अ̱जस्य̱ नाभा̱ अध्येक̱मर्पि̍त̱ं यस्मि̱न् विश्वा̍नि̱ भुव̍नानि त̱स्थुः
164.m: That very embryo the waters held as the first, wherein all the gods gathered together. / Fixed upon the navel of the Unborn was the One, in which all worlds stood.

164.s: na taṃ vi̍dātha̱ ya i̱mā ja̱jānā̱nyadyu̱ṣmāka̱manta̍raṃ babhūva nī̱hā̱reṇa̱ prāvṛ̍tā jalpyā̍ cāsu̱tṛpa̍ uktha̱śāsa̍ścaranti
164.d: न तं वि̍दाथ̱ य इ̱मा ज̱जाना̱न्यद्यु̱ष्माक̱मन्त̍रं बभूव नी̱हा̱रेण̱ प्रावृ̍ता जल्प्या̍ चासु̱तृप̍ उक्थ̱शास̍श्चरन्ति
164.m: You do not know him who generated these [worlds]; another thing has come between you. / Enveloped in mist and babble, the life-delighters wander reciting hymns.

164.s: vi̱śvaka̍rmā̱ hyaja̍niṣṭa de̱va ādidga̍ndha̱rvo a̍bhavad dvi̱tīya̍ḥ tṛ̱tīya̍ḥ pi̱tā ja̍ni̱tauṣa̍dhīnā̱mapā̱ṃ garbha̱ṃ vya̍dadhātpuru̱trā
164.d: वि̱श्वक̍र्मा̱ ह्यज̍निष्ट दे̱व आदिद्ग̍न्ध̱र्वो अ̍भवद् द्वि̱तीय̍ः तृ̱तीय̍ः पि̱ता ज̍नि̱तौष̍धीना̱मपा̱ं गर्भ̱ं व्य̍दधात्पुरु̱त्रा
164.m: For Viśvakarman was born as god; thereupon the Gandharva became the second. / The third was father, generator of plants; he placed the embryo of the waters in many places.
